text.en: Meena saw a green fuzz on stale bread. "Tiny living things grew there," her teacher said.

Microbes are tiny organisms seen only under a microscope. The main groups are bacteria, viruses, fungi and prions. A fungus has a body called a thallus, which is a mycelium in multicellular forms. Fungi living on living hosts are parasites and those on dead matter are saprophytes.
Microbes are useful. Biofertilisers enrich the soil, microbes are used in industries such as making curd and bread, and in medicine such as antibiotics. They also cause diseases. The gap between infection and the first sign of disease is the incubation period.
Airborne diseases spread through the air, waterborne through unclean water, and vector-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue, chikungunya and filaria through mosquitoes. AIDS and hepatitis-B are among the diseases spread by other routes. Immunisation with vaccines gives protection.
